findings.finding: Child preexec reports os.readlink(/proc/self) via an inherited pipe. The parent validates numeric identity and reads that host-visible proc status. It does not derive RSS/VmSize/HWM from namespace-local Popen.pid.

RSS/cgroup sampling retains the reviewed limits. killpg(proc.pid) uses the caller namespace process-group ID created by start_new_session; Popen.poll/wait use the real child object. Host /proc identifiers must not replace syscall IDs.
Admission uses global cgroup nonreclaimable accounting and static reservations, never summed process RSS or /proc/<Popen.pid>. Namespace-local PID confusion does not affect those memory observations.
Popen start_new_session, poll/wait and killpg use namespace-correct child process identifiers; no direct proc path is consulted.

limits: Existing sampled-RSS/cgroup and static-admission limitations remain; no new hard physical-memory guarantee.
This review addresses the observed PID-namespace mismatch only. It neither runs a checker nor changes existing timeout/address-space/physical-budget/reserve values.
No proof acceptance, compiler launch, process signal or code/runtime/control mutation.
recommendation: Keep reviewed829d/e04 and builder349a unchanged. Restrict the optional supervisor02 change to operational process-identity metadata.
